title: Fishhawk crew message (crew-message-v1)
description: A typed, addressed message one crew role sends another, implementing ADR-081 (#3727) rules 1-3. NOT a plan ArtifactKind: it is a standalone contract with its own schema and its own Go package (backend/internal/crewmessage), so plan-standard-v1 stays frozen and a crew message never routes through the plan validator. A message is ADVICE, NEVER AN ORDER (rule 2): the shape below can express a question, an observation, a request or an escalation, and it deliberately cannot express a scope path, a constraint, a delegation or a gate outcome — every object closes with additionalProperties:false and no property name anywhere is drawn from the authority vocabulary. Addresses are ROLES, never model instances (rule 3): sender_role and recipient_role draw from a closed enum, so a model identifier or an agent instance name is structurally unaddressable. SCHEMA-ONLY VALIDATION IS NOT SUFFICIENT: the crew-role enum admits 'implementer' because the implementer is a real crew role and a legal SENDER, so this schema ALONE accepts recipient_role: implementer. ARCHITECTURE section 6 invariant #8 (no message is ever delivered to an implement stage) is enforced ONLY by the Go validator crewmessage.Validate, which is the single source of truth for addressability. Every consumer MUST call it; a bare check-jsonschema run does not enforce that rule.

schema_version.description: Contract discriminator and version. A future major is a new schema file (crew-message-v2.schema.json) with its own const, never a break in place.

type.description: The closed five-member type set of ADR-081 rule 1. A consult asks a question and is answered synchronously in-process; a finding records an observation and is NOT a concern (it never enters the merge gate); a work_request asks for an item to be filed and never dispatches a run; a notice informs and expects no answer; an escalation surfaces a disagreement to the captain and produces binding text only once the captain answers. The enum selects the payload shape via the allOf if/then arms below.

sender_role.description: The role that sent the message. On the wire the server DERIVES this from the token's executing stage and never reads it from a request body (ADR-081 rule 3); the field exists so a stored or rendered message is self-describing.

recipient_role.description: The role the message is addressed to. Invariant #8 forbids addressing a role an implement stage executes; that rule is NOT expressed here (the enum admits implementer as a legal sender) and lives in crewmessage.CanReceive.

payload.description: The typed body. Deliberately declares NO constraint of its own: the type enum above admits only the five members, so exactly one allOf arm below always fires and narrows payload to that type's closed object $def. Declaring type:object here as well would be redundant and would make this the one object-typed subschema in the document that cannot close (closing it would forbid every payload field), which is why TestSchema_ClosedAtEveryLevel finds no exception to walk around.

evidence.description: Optional references grounding the message in recorded state. Deliberately carries NO repo-path or code-location member: a path list is the nearest thing this contract has to a scope expression, and rule 2 forbids a field that can express scope. Cite a file in a payload prose field, which carries no authority.

response_required.description: Whether the sender is waiting on an answer. Declared as a plain boolean on EVERY type here; ADR-081 D1 answers only consult and escalation synchronously, so response_required on any other type is an unanswerable request and is rejected by crewmessage.Validate (ErrResponseNotAnswerable), not by this schema.

deadline.description: Optional RFC 3339 instant after which the sender stops waiting. An unanswered consult times out to 'no answer' and never blocks the stage (ADR-081 rule 6).

crew-role.description: The closed crew vocabulary (ADR-081 rules 3 and 8, plus E78's plan-fit reviewer persona). An ENUM, never a free string, so a model identifier ('claude-opus-5') or an agent instance name can never be an address. 'implementer' is a member ON PURPOSE: the implementer is a real crew role and a legal sender_role. What invariant #8 forbids is ADDRESSING one, and that refusal lives in crewmessage.CanReceive so it is a live, testable control rather than dead code masked by a narrower enum. Adding an eighth role is an additive change within this major.

anchor.description: Exactly one of the three anchors. All three members are declared optional and the oneOf below admits precisely one: a document carrying none matches zero arms, and a document carrying two or three matches more than one, so both are rejected.

run_id.description: A Fishhawk run this message is about. Anchors the message on that run's audit chain partition.

issue_ref.description: A work item, e.g. "kuhlman-labs/fishhawk#3735". Anchors a run-less message on the account's global chain.

decision_record_id.description: A settled decision, e.g. "ADR-081". The historian's precedent query and the architect's contradiction check both anchor here.

evidence-reference.description: One pointer into recorded state. The kind enum is closed and deliberately omits any file/path member (see the evidence property above).

kind.description: What sort of thing ref names.

ref.description: The identifier or URL, interpreted per kind.

consult-payload.description: A question one role asks another, answered synchronously in-process (ADR-081 D1 option 1). The canonical first use is planner -> historian (rule 8).

question.description: The question, stated directly to the recipient role.

what_i_can_infer.description: Optional. What the sender already established on its own, narrowing the question to the part it genuinely cannot answer.

context.description: Optional prose framing. Prose only — it confers no authority and binds nothing.

finding-payload.description: An observation one role wants another to see. A finding is NOT a concern: it never enters the merge gate and nothing is blocked by it. If the captain wants one acted on they route it explicitly (ADR-081 rule 2).

severity.description: Optional sender-assessed severity. Advisory: it feeds no gate and changes no outcome.

work-request-payload.description: A request that a work item be filed. Filing goes through the existing applyAndFileWorkItem path, run-scoped, and NEVER dispatches a run (ADR-081 rule 2).

rationale.description: Optional. Why it is worth filing now.

notice-payload.description: Information delivered with no answer expected, asynchronously (ADR-081 D1 option 3).

escalation-payload.description: A disagreement surfaced to the captain once the bounded round count is exhausted (ADR-081 D3 option 1). recommended_default and tradeoffs are declared here as optional properties and made REQUIRED by the escalation if/then arm above, mirroring the clarification-request calibration rule: the captain must be able to accept the default at a glance. Escalation text becomes binding only once the captain answers.

recommended_default.description: What the sender would do absent a ruling. Required on an escalation by the arm above.

tradeoffs.description: The consequences of the recommended default versus the alternatives. Required on an escalation by the arm above.
